citations.narrative:
In the guinea pig room, there was a moderate to heavy accumulation of dirt and dust on several areas of the ceiling and
along the surfaces of all the walls in this room. There were several cobwebs along the corners of the walls and ceiling and
around the windows. At least one large cobweb measured approximately 1ftX 2ft in size. Additionally, there was an
approximately 2ft to 3ft section of ceiling panels in this room which has become detached and is loosely, bent downward.
Accumulations of dirt, dust and cobwebs in any area where animals are housed may negatively impact the health and
well-being of the animals including possible respiratory problems, attracting pests, and other disease hazards.
Additionally, a ceiling in the animal room in disrepair may pose a risk of injury or other hazard from loose materials falling
on the animal enclosures below.
Premises (buildings and grounds) must be kept clean and in good repair in order to protect the animals from injury and to
facilitate the prescribed husbandry practices set forth in this subpart.
Correct by 10/27/2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
